main.content:
==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|immediatly}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|immediate|ly|id2=adverbial}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈmiː.di.ət.li/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈmi.di.ɪt.li/|/əˈmi.di.ət.li/|a=GA,CA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-immediately.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈmiː.d͡ʒət.li/|/əˈmiː.d͡ʒət.li/|a=colloquial}}
* {{hyphenation|en|im|me|di|ate|ly}}, {{hyphenation|en|im|me|diate|ly|nocaption=1}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# In an [[immediate]] manner; [[instantly]] or without [[delay]].
#: {{ux|en|I hope we can begin '''immediately'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en
|year=1967
|author=w:Barbara Sleigh
|title=w:Jessamy
|year_published=1993
|location=Sevenoaks, Kent
|publisher=Bloomsbury
|isbn=0 340 19547 9
|page=96
|url=
|passage=His unruly hair was slicked down with water, and as Jessamy introduced him to Miss Brindle his face assumed a cherubic innocence which would '''immediately''' have aroused the suspicions of anyone who knew him.
}}
#* {{quote-journal|en
|date=November 12, 2011
|author=
|title=International friendly: England 1-0 Spain
|work=BBC Sport
|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15693231.stm
|page=
|passage=Spain failed to move through the gears despite exerting control for lengthy spells and a measure of perspective must be applied '''immediately''' to the outcome.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120201060013/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15693231.stm|archivedate=1 February 2012}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}<!-- Please no more than 3–4 quotes here, further quotes only in 'Citations' (see [[WT:QUOTE]])-->
# Without any intervening time or space.

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|forthwith}}, {{l|en|now}}, {{l|en|right away}}, {{l|en|straightaway}}, {{l|en|tout de suite}}, {{l|en|directly}}; see also [[Thesaurus:immediately]]

===Conjunction===

#: {{ux|en|My dog is an [[open book#Noun|open book]]: '''immediately''' he smelled our dinner, he grew more interested in our activities.}}

|passage='''Immediately''' he ''saw'' the firm, he realised what he could do.}}
